title: Sable and the Alibi
premise: Retired detective Tamsin Ravensworth receives a confession letter for the murder of Edmund Vane, postmarked the day after his funeral, naming Tamsin as the only person who can 'finish it properly.' The letter's details match a cold case Tamsin never closed — one that cost them their career and their marriage. As Tamsin reopens the file, they discover the confessor is being protected by an alibi so airtight it could only have been constructed by someone with access to the original investigation. The killer is Edmund's heir, who has spent years studying the case to bury the truth beneath Tamsin's own documented mistakes. At the anniversary dinner, Tamsin springs a trap built on the alibi's single unrepeatable detail, forcing a confession before the assembled family, and chooses truth over loyalty at last.
about_author: Jude Zhou is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unsolved case files before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the weight of unfinished business from a coastal town that looks suspiciously like home.

chapters.title: Postmarked After
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A confession letter arrives for a murder Tamsin failed to solve twenty years ago, postmarked the day after Edmund Vane's funeral. The handwriting is unfamiliar; the details are not. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in reluctant recognition as old failure resurfaces in the bookshop's quiet.

chapters.title: The File That Ruined Me
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with flashback. Tamsin retrieves the boxed case file from storage and relives the investigation that ended their career: a missing witness, a coerced statement, a suspect who died before trial. Emotional beat: shame curdling into resolve to finally close what was left open.

chapters.title: Heirs and Apparents
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Under pretext of condolence, Tamsin visits Vane House and meets the heirs: widow Cressida, son Julian, and niece Wren, who seems to know too much about the old case. Emotional beat: surface grief over a current of watchfulness — everyone performing innocence.

chapters.title: Airtight
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The confession letter's timeline collapses against Julian's documented alibi — verified by police records Tamsin themselves filed two decades ago. Only someone inside the investigation could have built it. Emotional beat: paranoia; the trap may have been set for Tamsin specifically.

chapters.title: What Wren Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren admits she found her uncle's hidden notebooks — annotated copies of the case file — and confesses she sent the letter hoping someone would finally look. Emotional beat: guilt and relief entwined; loyalty to family cracking against love of truth.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Waited
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin tracks down Dolores Finch, the witness whose statement was buried, now dying and willing to talk. She reveals Edmund knew his killer and stayed silent to protect the inheritance. Emotional beat: tenderness toward a stranger bound by the same old wound.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Invited to the one-year memorial dinner, Tamsin realizes the killer expects them there — the invitation is bait or a taunt. They quietly verify the alibi's one fragile hinge: a phone call logged at 9:47 p.m. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing fear; the hunter decides to be hunted.

chapters.title: Glass Raised
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the dinner, Tamsin recounts the case aloud, watching faces. When they mention the 9:47 call, Cressida's glass trembles — the call was placed from the boathouse, where no phone existed after renovations. Emotional beat: taut suspense; the room becomes an interrogation chamber.

chapters.title: The Confession Proper
chapters.summary: Cressida's POV. Cornered by the impossible detail, Cressida confesses: Edmund discovered she'd forged his will and threatened to disinherit Julian; she killed him and built her alibi from Tamsin's own case notes, stolen years ago. Emotional beat: venomous grief — she loved the house more than the man.

chapters.title: Closing the File
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Arrest made, Tamsin returns to the bookshop, writes FINISHED across the old case folder, and offers Wren a job among the shelves. Emotional beat: quiet peace — belonging found not in the past closed, but in the life continued.
